approaches_tried.approach: Naive string concatenation of chunk_*.md files (no separator) for the Criterion 1 offline replay
approaches_tried.reason: The on-disk corpus markdown for both named papers exists only as overlapping RAG-indexing chunk_*.md fragments (not literature-convert.sh's single-file .md output, which no longer exists on disk), each prefixed with a per-chunk citation header line (e.g. 'Ishtiaq Ohearn 2001 ...'). Concatenating file contents with no separator glued the end of one chunk directly to the next chunk's header line, producing 7 spurious [a-z].[A-Z] hits unrelated to the real fix (residue 7 instead of 0 for ishtiaq_ohearn_2001). Joining chunks with '\n\n' instead reproduced the research report's exact raw counts (4 and 7) and the expected post-fix residue of 0 for both papers.

objective_2_criterion_1.method: read-only concatenation (newline-joined) of existing chunk_*.md files under ~/Projects/Literature/{doc}/, no reconversion, no writes
